questions.question: The inner and outer radii of two concentric circles are 6.7 cm and 9.5 cm, respectively. What is the difference between their circumferences (in cm) ? Take π = 22/7
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Inner radius of concentric circles = 6.7cm

Outer radius of concentric circles = 9.5 cm

**Formula:**

Circumference of circle = 2πr

**Calculation:**

Circumference of small circle = π × 2 × 6.7 = 13.4π

Circumference of big circle = π × 2 × 9.5 = 19π

**∴ Difference between their circumference = (19 - 13.4)π = 5.6 × 22/7 = 17.6 cm**

questions.question:
The string of a kite is 158 m long and it makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. What is the height (in m) of the kite ?

Assume there is no slack in the string.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** triangle, the side opposite to **30°** is half of the **hypotenuse**.

Given **Hypotenuse (String)** = 158 m.

**Height** = 158 ÷ 2 = 79 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 79 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19f977879377709bd745969ce484f88cb296c794e3fe010e4bbd11d2c101bba1.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the **string (Hypotenuse AC)** = 158 m

**Angle of elevation (θ)** = 30°

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = **Perpendicular (Height)** ÷ **Hypotenuse (String)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin 30° = h ÷ 158

⇒ 1/2 = h ÷ 158

⇒ h = 158 ÷ 2

⇒ h = 79 m

**∴ The correct answer is 79 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Common values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, sin 60° = √3/2.

30°−60°−90° Triangle Rule

The sides are always in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2 corresponding to the angles 30° : 60° : 90°.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking upwards at an object.</p

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs. 1,170, Elisa suffers as much loss as she would have gained by selling it at a profit of 22%. If she sells it for Rs. 1,450, then her profit/loss per cent (correct up to one decimal place) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100%.

As **Loss** equals profit of 22%, the first **Selling Price (SP)** = 100% − 22% = 78%.

⇒ 78% = ₹1,170 ⇒ 100% = (1,170 ÷ 78) × 100 = ₹1,500.

New **SP** = ₹1,450 ⇒ **Loss** = 1,500 − 1,450 = ₹50.

**Loss%** = (50 ÷ 1500) × 100 = 3.33... ≈ 3.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss, 3.3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**SP₁** = ₹1,170

**Profit%** (for comparison) = 22%

**SP₂** = ₹1,450

**Formula Used:**

**Loss** = **CP** − **SP** | **Profit** = **SP** − **CP** | **Loss%** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0db9d80a554cb9cb66f71e55eba0ba1de0212fe2f6701d0ec45aaa67620b1d45.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Cost Price** of the article be x.

According to the question, **Loss** at ₹1,170 = **Profit** at 22%.

⇒ x − 1,170 = 22% of x

⇒ x − 1,170 = 0.22x

⇒ x − 0.22x = 1,170

⇒ 0.78x = 1,170

⇒ x = 1,170 ÷ 0.78 = 1,500

The **Cost Price (CP)** is ₹1,500.

Now, if the article is sold for ₹1,450 (**SP₂**):

⇒ **Loss** = CP − SP₂ = 1,500 − 1,450 = ₹50

⇒ **Loss%** = (50 ÷ 1,500) × 100

⇒ **Loss%** = 10 ÷ 3 = 3.33...

Rounding to one decimal place, we get 3.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss, 3.3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100. Use these to find SP directly from CP and percentage change.

Cost Price as Base

Assuming CP = 100 units simplifies calculations. A 22% profit makes SP = 122 units, while a 22% loss makes SP = 78 units.

questions.question: What is the greatest five-digit number that is completely divisible by 8, 15, 16, 21 and 5?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 8, 15, 16, 21, and 5 is 1680.

Check options for divisibility by 1680 (must be divisible by factors 7, 16, and 3).

99120 ÷ 16 = 6195; 99120 ÷ 3 (sum of digits 21) is true; 99120 ÷ 7 = 14160.

Since 99120 is the largest option divisible by 1680, it is the required number.

**∴ The correct answer is 99120.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are 8, 15, 16, 21, 5; Target is the greatest 5-digit number.

**Formula Used:** Required Number = LCM(8, 15, 16, 21, 5) × k ≤ 99999.

 
 
• 
 
•

 Greatest Divisible: 99120
 Multiples of LCM (1680)

⇒ Prime factorization of divisors:

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 16 = 2⁴

⇒ 21 = 3 × 7

⇒ 5 = 5

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 16 × 15 × 7 = 1680

⇒ Divide the largest 5-digit number (99999) by 1680:

⇒ 99999 ÷ 1680 = 59 with remainder 879

⇒ Required number = 99999 − 879 = 99120

**∴ The correct answer is 99120.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Divisibility Rule of 16

A number is divisible by 16 if the last four digits of the number are divisible by 16.

Finding Greatest N-digit Number

To find the greatest N-digit number divisible by x, divide the largest possible N-digit number (9...9) by x and subtract the remainder.</p

questions.question: A boat can travel with a speed of 19 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, then what will be the total time (in hours) taken by the boat to go 88 km downstream and 24 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water = 19kmph

Speed of stream = 3kmph

**Formula:**

Downstream speed = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

Upstream speed = Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream

**Calculation:**

Downstream speed = 19 + 3 = 22 kmph

Upstream speed = 19 - 3 = 16kmph

Required time = 88/22 + 24/16 = 4 + 3/2 = 5.5

**∴ total time (in hours) taken by the boat to go 88 km downstream and 24 km upstream is 5.5 hours.**

**Calculation:**

Volume of cylinder = πh × (9)²

⇒ h = 2.058

⇒ h = 2.1 cm(nearest value)

**∴ Height of cylinder is 2.1cm**

questions.question: A man invests Rs. 7,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 2 years and Rs. 10,000 at compound interest at the same rate for the same period, compounded annually. What will be the total interest and the total amount (in Rs.) respectively, on maturity?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs.7000

Rate of interest = 8%

Time = 2 years

**Formula:**

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

SI = PNR/100

CI = P(1 + R/100)² - P

**Calculation:**

SI = 7000 × 8 × 2/100 = Rs.1120

Amount after SI = 7000 + 1120 = Rs.8120

CI = 10000(1 + 8/100)² - 10000 = Rs.1664

Amount after CI = 10000 + 1664 = Rs.11664

**∴ Total amount after maturity = 8120 + 11664 = Rs.19784**

**Total interest after 2 years = 1120 + 1664 = Rs.2784**

questions.question: One-fifth of a journey is covered at a speed of 30 km/h, one-fourth of the journey at a speed of 25 km/h and the rest at 60 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h, correct to one decimal place) for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1/5 of journey = 30kmph

1/4 of journey = 25kmph

(1 - 1/5 - 1/4 = 11/20) of journey = 60kmph

**Formula:**

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

**Calculation:**

Let total distance of journey be a km.

Time taken for 1/5 of journey = a/150 hours

Time taken for 1/4 of journey = a/100 hours

Time taken for 11/20 of journey = 11a/1200 hours

Total time taken for a km = a/150 + a/100 + 11a/1200 = 31a/1200 hours

**∴ Average speed = a/(31a/1200) = 38.7kmph**

questions.question: If ( x + (1)/(x) )³ = 27, then what is the value of ( x² + (1)/(x²) ) ? Given that x is real.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

( x + (1)/(x) )³ = 27,

( x + (1)/(x) ) = sqrt[3]{27} = 3

**Formula:**

(a + b) = a² + b² + ab

**Calculation:**

( x + (1)/(x) ) = 3

Squaring both the sides, we get

( x + (1)/(x) )² = 3²

⇒ x² + (1)/(x²) + 2 . x².(1)/(x²) = 9

⇒ ( x² + (1)/(x²) ) = 9 - 2 = 7

**∴ The value of ( x² + (1)/(x²) ) = 7**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**If ( x + (1)/(x) ) = a , then ( x² + (1)/(x²) ) = a² - 2

⇒ ( x + (1)/(x) ) = 3, then ( x² + (1)/(x²) ) = 3² - 2 = 9 - 2 = 7
